doc.md:
Assists in creating [`RenderNode`](xref:gtk:Gsk.RenderNode)s for widgets.

It functions in a similar way to a cairo context, and maintains a stack
of render nodes and their associated transformations.

The node at the top of the stack is the one that `gtk_snapshot_append_…()`
functions operate on. Use the `gtk_snapshot_push_…()` functions and
[`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Snapshot#method:pop) to change the current node.

The typical way to obtain a `GtkSnapshot` object is as an argument to
the [`Widget.snapshot()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#vfunc:snapshot) vfunc. If you need to create your own
`GtkSnapshot`, use [`Snapshot.new()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#constructor:new).

Note that `GtkSnapshot` applies some optimizations, so the node
it produces may not match the API calls 1:1. For example, it will
omit clip nodes if the child node is entirely contained within the
clip rectangle.

append_border.brief: Appends a stroked border rectangle inside the given `outline`.
append_border.md:
Appends a stroked border rectangle inside the given `outline`.

The four sides of the border can have different widths and colors.

append_cairo.brief: Creates a new [`CairoNode`](xref:gtk:Gsk.CairoNode) and appends it to the current render node of `snapshot`, without changing the current node.
append_cairo.md:
Creates a new [`CairoNode`](xref:gtk:Gsk.CairoNode) and appends it to the current
render node of `snapshot`, without changing the current node.

append_color.brief: Creates a new render node drawing the `color` into the given `bounds` and appends it to the current render node of `snapshot`.
append_color.md:
Creates a new render node drawing the `color` into the
given `bounds` and appends it to the current render node
of `snapshot`.

You should try to avoid calling this function if
`color` is transparent.

append_conic_gradient.brief: Appends a conic gradient node with the given stops to `snapshot`.
append_conic_gradient.md: Appends a conic gradient node with the given stops to `snapshot`.

append_fill.brief: A convenience method to fill a path with a color.
append_fill.md:
A convenience method to fill a path with a color.

See [`Snapshot.push_fill()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:push_fill) if you need
to fill a path with more complex content than
a color.

append_inset_shadow.brief: Appends an inset shadow into the box given by `outline`.
append_inset_shadow.md: Appends an inset shadow into the box given by `outline`.

append_layout.brief: Creates render nodes for rendering `layout` in the given foregound `color` and appends them to the current node of `snapshot` without changing the current node.
append_layout.md:
Creates render nodes for rendering `layout` in the given foregound `color`
and appends them to the current node of `snapshot` without changing the
current node. The current theme's foreground color for a widget can be
obtained with [`Widget.get_color()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:get_color).

Note that if the layout does not produce any visible output, then nodes
may not be added to the `snapshot`.

append_linear_gradient.brief: Appends a linear gradient node with the given stops to `snapshot`.
append_linear_gradient.md: Appends a linear gradient node with the given stops to `snapshot`.

append_node.brief: Appends `node` to the current render node of `snapshot`, without changing the current node.
append_node.md:
Appends `node` to the current render node of `snapshot`,
without changing the current node.

If `snapshot` does not have a current node yet, `node`
will become the initial node.

append_outset_shadow.brief: Appends an outset shadow node around the box given by `outline`.
append_outset_shadow.md: Appends an outset shadow node around the box given by `outline`.

append_paste.brief: Creates a new render node that pastes the contents copied by a previous call to [`Snapshot.push_copy()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:push_copy)
append_paste.md:
Creates a new render node that pastes the contents
copied by a previous call to [`Snapshot.push_copy()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:push_copy)

append_radial_gradient.brief: Appends a radial gradient node with the given stops to `snapshot`.
append_radial_gradient.md: Appends a radial gradient node with the given stops to `snapshot`.

append_repeating_linear_gradient.brief: Appends a repeating linear gradient node with the given stops to `snapshot`.
append_repeating_linear_gradient.md: Appends a repeating linear gradient node with the given stops to `snapshot`.

append_repeating_radial_gradient.brief: Appends a repeating radial gradient node with the given stops to `snapshot`.
append_repeating_radial_gradient.md: Appends a repeating radial gradient node with the given stops to `snapshot`.

append_scaled_texture.brief: Creates a new render node drawing the `texture` into the given `bounds` and appends it to the current render node of `snapshot`.
append_scaled_texture.md:
Creates a new render node drawing the `texture`
into the given `bounds` and appends it to the
current render node of `snapshot`.

In contrast to [`Snapshot.append_texture()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:append_texture),
this function provides control about how the filter
that is used when scaling.

append_stroke.brief: A convenience method to stroke a path with a color.
append_stroke.md:
A convenience method to stroke a path with a color.

See [`Snapshot.push_stroke()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:push_stroke) if you need
to stroke a path with more complex content than
a color.

append_texture.brief: Creates a new render node drawing the `texture` into the given `bounds` and appends it to the current render node of `snapshot`.
append_texture.md:
Creates a new render node drawing the `texture`
into the given `bounds` and appends it to the
current render node of `snapshot`.

If the texture needs to be scaled to fill `bounds`,
linear filtering is used. See [`Snapshot.append_scaled_texture()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:append_scaled_texture)
if you need other filtering, such as nearest-neighbour.

free_to_node.brief: Returns the node that was constructed by `snapshot` and frees `snapshot`.
free_to_node.md:
Returns the node that was constructed by `snapshot`
and frees `snapshot`.

See also [`Snapshot.to_node()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:to_node).

free_to_paintable.brief: Returns a paintable for the node that was constructed by `snapshot` and frees `snapshot`.
free_to_paintable.md:
Returns a paintable for the node that was
constructed by `snapshot` and frees `snapshot`.

gl_shader_pop_texture.brief: Removes the top element from the stack of render nodes and adds it to the nearest [`GLShaderNode`](xref:gtk:Gsk.GLShaderNode) below it.
gl_shader_pop_texture.deprecated_md:
GTK's new Vulkan-focused rendering
  does not support this feature. Use [`GLArea`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea) for
  OpenGL rendering.
gl_shader_pop_texture.md:
Removes the top element from the stack of render nodes and
adds it to the nearest [`GLShaderNode`](xref:gtk:Gsk.GLShaderNode) below it.

This must be called the same number of times as the number
of textures is needed for the shader in
[`Snapshot.push_gl_shader()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:push_gl_shader).

perspective.md:
Applies a perspective projection transform.

See [`Transform.perspective()`](xref:gtk:Gsk.Transform#method:perspective) for a discussion on the details.

pop.brief: Removes the top element from the stack of render nodes, and appends it to the node underneath it.
pop.md:
Removes the top element from the stack of render nodes,
and appends it to the node underneath it.

push_blend.brief: Blends together two images with the given blend mode.
push_blend.md:
Blends together two images with the given blend mode.

Until the first call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop), the
bottom image for the blend operation will be recorded.
After that call, the top image to be blended will be
recorded until the second call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

Calling this function requires two subsequent calls
to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_blur.md:
Blurs an image.

The image is recorded until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_clip.brief: Clips an image to a rectangle.
push_clip.md:
Clips an image to a rectangle.

The image is recorded until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_color_matrix.brief: Modifies the colors of an image by applying an affine transformation in RGB space.
push_color_matrix.md:
Modifies the colors of an image by applying an affine transformation
in RGB space.

In particular, the colors will be transformed by applying

    pixel = transpose(color_matrix) * pixel + color_offset

for every pixel. The transformation operates on unpremultiplied
colors, with color components ordered R, G, B, A.

The image is recorded until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_component_transfer.brief: Modifies the colors of an image by applying a transfer function for each component.
push_component_transfer.md:
Modifies the colors of an image by applying a transfer
function for each component.

The transfer functions operate on unpremultiplied colors.

The image is recorded until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_composite.brief: Until the first call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop), the mask image for the mask operation will be recorded.
push_composite.md:
Until the first call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop), the
mask image for the mask operation will be recorded.

After that call, the child image will be recorded until
the second call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

Calling this function requires 2 subsequent calls to gtk_snapshot_pop().

push_copy.brief: Stores the current rendering state for later pasting via [`Snapshot.append_paste()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:append_paste).
push_copy.md:
Stores the current rendering state for later pasting via
[`Snapshot.append_paste()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:append_paste).

Pasting is possible until the matching call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_cross_fade.brief: Snapshots a cross-fade operation between two images with the given `progress`.
push_cross_fade.md:
Snapshots a cross-fade operation between two images with the
given `progress`.

Until the first call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop), the start image
will be snapshot. After that call, the end image will be recorded
until the second call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

Calling this function requires two subsequent calls
to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_debug.brief: Inserts a debug node with a message.
push_debug.md:
Inserts a debug node with a message.

Debug nodes don't affect the rendering at all, but can be
helpful in identifying parts of a render node tree dump,
for example in the GTK inspector.

push_fill.brief: Fills the area given by `path` and `fill_rule` with an image and discards everything outside of it.
push_fill.md:
Fills the area given by `path` and `fill_rule` with an image and discards everything
outside of it.

The image is recorded until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

If you want to fill the path with a color, [`Snapshot.append_fill()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:append_fill)
than rendering new ones, use [`Snapshot.append_fill()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:append_fill)
may be more convenient.

push_gl_shader.deprecated_md:
GTK's new Vulkan-focused rendering
  does not support this feature. Use [`GLArea`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea) for
  OpenGL rendering.
push_gl_shader.md:
Push a [`GLShaderNode`](xref:gtk:Gsk.GLShaderNode).

The node uses the given [`GLShader`](xref:gtk:Gsk.GLShader) and uniform values
Additionally this takes a list of `n_children` other nodes
which will be passed to the [`GLShaderNode`](xref:gtk:Gsk.GLShaderNode).

The `take_args` argument is a block of data to use for uniform
arguments, as per types and offsets defined by the `shader`.
Normally this is generated by [`GLShader.format_args()`](xref:gtk:Gsk.GLShader#method:format_args)
or [`ShaderArgsBuilder`](xref:gtk:Gsk.ShaderArgsBuilder).

The snapshotter takes ownership of `take_args`, so the caller should
not free it after this.

If the renderer doesn't support GL shaders, or if there is any
problem when compiling the shader, then the node will draw pink.
You should use [`GLShader.compile()`](xref:gtk:Gsk.GLShader#method:compile) to ensure the `shader`
will work for the renderer before using it.

If the shader requires textures (see [`GLShader.get_n_textures()`](xref:gtk:Gsk.GLShader#method:get_n_textures)),
then it is expected that you call [`Snapshot.gl_shader_pop_texture()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:gl_shader_pop_texture)
the number of times that are required. Each of these calls will generate
a node that is added as a child to the `GskGLShaderNode`, which in turn
will render these offscreen and pass as a texture to the shader.

Once all textures (if any) are pop:ed, you must call the regular
[`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

If you want to use pre-existing textures as input to the shader rather
than rendering new ones, use [`Snapshot.append_texture()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:append_texture) to
push a texture node. These will be used directly rather than being
re-rendered.

For details on how to write shaders, see [`GLShader`](xref:gtk:Gsk.GLShader).

push_isolation.brief: Isolates the following drawing operations from previous ones.
push_isolation.md:
Isolates the following drawing operations from previous ones.

You can express "everything but these flags" in a forward compatible
way by using bit math:
`GSK_ISOLATION_ALL & ~(GSK_ISOLATION_BACKGROUND | GSK_ISOLATION_COPY_PASTE)`
will isolate everything but background and copy/paste.

For what isolation features exist, see [`Isolation`](xref:gtk:Gsk.Isolation).

Content is isolated until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_mask.brief: Until the first call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop), the mask image for the mask operation will be recorded.
push_mask.md:
Until the first call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop), the
mask image for the mask operation will be recorded.

After that call, the source image will be recorded until
the second call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

Calling this function requires 2 subsequent calls to gtk_snapshot_pop().

push_opacity.brief: Modifies the opacity of an image.
push_opacity.md:
Modifies the opacity of an image.

The image is recorded until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_repeat.brief: Creates a node that repeats the child node.
push_repeat.md:
Creates a node that repeats the child node.

The child is recorded until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_rounded_clip.brief: Clips an image to a rounded rectangle.
push_rounded_clip.md:
Clips an image to a rounded rectangle.

The image is recorded until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_shadow.brief: Applies a shadow to an image.
push_shadow.md:
Applies a shadow to an image.

The image is recorded until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

push_stroke.brief: Strokes the given `path` with the attributes given by `stroke` and an image.
push_stroke.md:
Strokes the given `path` with the attributes given by `stroke` and
an image.

The image is recorded until the next call to [`Snapshot.pop()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:pop).

Note that the strokes are subject to the same transformation as
everything else, so uneven scaling will cause horizontal and vertical
strokes to have different widths.

If you want to stroke the path with a color, [`Snapshot.append_stroke()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:append_stroke)
may be more convenient.

render_background.brief: Creates a render node for the CSS background according to `context`, and appends it to the current node of `snapshot`, without changing the current node.
render_background.md:
Creates a render node for the CSS background according to `context`,
and appends it to the current node of `snapshot`, without changing
the current node.

render_focus.brief: Creates a render node for the focus outline according to `context`, and appends it to the current node of `snapshot`, without changing the current node.
render_focus.md:
Creates a render node for the focus outline according to `context`,
and appends it to the current node of `snapshot`, without changing
the current node.

render_frame.brief: Creates a render node for the CSS border according to `context`, and appends it to the current node of `snapshot`, without changing the current node.
render_frame.md:
Creates a render node for the CSS border according to `context`,
and appends it to the current node of `snapshot`, without changing
the current node.

render_insertion_cursor.brief: Draws a text caret using `snapshot` at the specified index of `layout`.
render_insertion_cursor.md: Draws a text caret using `snapshot` at the specified index of `layout`.

render_layout.brief: Creates a render node for rendering `layout` according to the style information in `context`, and appends it to the current node of `snapshot`, without changing the current node.
render_layout.md:
Creates a render node for rendering `layout` according to the style
information in `context`, and appends it to the current node of `snapshot`,
without changing the current node.

restore.brief: Restores `snapshot` to the state saved by a preceding call to [`Snapshot.save()`](xref:gtk:Snapshot#method:save) and removes that state from the stack of saved states.
restore.md:
Restores `snapshot` to the state saved by a preceding call to
[`Snapshot.save()`](xref:gtk:Snapshot#method:save) and removes that state from the stack of
saved states.

rotate.brief: Rotates @@snapshot's coordinate system by `angle` degrees in 2D space - or in 3D speak, rotates around the Z axis.
rotate.md:
Rotates @@snapshot's coordinate system by `angle` degrees in 2D space -
or in 3D speak, rotates around the Z axis. The rotation happens around
the origin point of (0, 0) in the `snapshot`'s current coordinate system.

To rotate around axes other than the Z axis, use [`Transform.rotate_3d()`](xref:gtk:Gsk.Transform#method:rotate_3d).

rotate_3d.brief: Rotates `snapshot`'s coordinate system by `angle` degrees around `axis`.
rotate_3d.md:
Rotates `snapshot`'s coordinate system by `angle` degrees around `axis`.

For a rotation in 2D space, use [`Transform.rotate()`](xref:gtk:Gsk.Transform#method:rotate).

save.brief: Makes a copy of the current state of `snapshot` and saves it on an internal stack.
save.md:
Makes a copy of the current state of `snapshot` and saves it
on an internal stack.

When [`Snapshot.restore()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:restore) is called, `snapshot` will
be restored to the saved state.

Multiple calls to [`Snapshot.save()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:save) and [`Snapshot.restore()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:restore)
can be nested; each call to `gtk_snapshot_restore()` restores the state from
the matching paired `gtk_snapshot_save()`.

It is necessary to clear all saved states with corresponding
calls to `gtk_snapshot_restore()`.

scale.brief: Scales `snapshot`'s coordinate system in 2-dimensional space by the given factors.
scale.md:
Scales `snapshot`'s coordinate system in 2-dimensional space by
the given factors.

Use [`Snapshot.scale_3d()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:scale_3d) to scale in all 3 dimensions.

scale_3d.brief: Scales `snapshot`'s coordinate system by the given factors.
scale_3d.md: Scales `snapshot`'s coordinate system by the given factors.

to_node.brief: Returns the render node that was constructed by `snapshot`.
to_node.md:
Returns the render node that was constructed
by `snapshot`.

Note that this function may return `NULL` if nothing has been
added to the snapshot or if its content does not produce pixels
to be rendered.

After calling this function, it is no longer possible to
add more nodes to `snapshot`. The only function that should
be called after this is [`Object.unref()`](xref:gtk:GObject.Object#method:unref).

to_paintable.brief: Returns a paintable encapsulating the render node that was constructed by `snapshot`.
to_paintable.md:
Returns a paintable encapsulating the render node
that was constructed by `snapshot`.

After calling this function, it is no longer possible to
add more nodes to `snapshot`. The only function that should
be called after this is [`Object.unref()`](xref:gtk:GObject.Object#method:unref).

transform.brief: Transforms `snapshot`'s coordinate system with the given `transform`.
transform.md: Transforms `snapshot`'s coordinate system with the given `transform`.

transform_matrix.brief: Transforms `snapshot`'s coordinate system with the given `matrix`.
transform_matrix.md: Transforms `snapshot`'s coordinate system with the given `matrix`.

translate.brief: Translates `snapshot`'s coordinate system by `point` in 2-dimensional space.
translate.md: Translates `snapshot`'s coordinate system by `point` in 2-dimensional space.
